column1: # claim-ledger.tsv — the §11.4.266 claim-vs-reality ledger for this repository.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
# No instrument in this tree compared a RECORDED CLAIM against the thing it
# describes. Nine instances were measured on 2026-09-07/08/09: a submodule
# primitive shipped upstream and nine tracked files went on asserting the gap
# for five days; three "actionable FAILs" that already existed; two gates
# PASSING over a stale ledger while the README showed a friendlier picture than
# the tree; a CLI flag recorded as unrecognised that had already landed; a
# database table recorded as empty that had already materialised.
# Every gate in this tree verifies its SUBJECT. Not one verified what the
# repository SAYS about its subject. §11.4.266 keys the enumeration from the
# CLAIM side, and this file is that enumeration.
# HOW A ROW STAYS HONEST — read this before adding one
# The failure this gate must not become is instance ten: a green gate over
# stale ground truth. Two rules keep it out.
#   1. A `prose` row stores NO measured figure. The CLAIMED value is read out
#      of the document at run time by the anchor's capture group; the REAL
#      value is re-measured by running the probe fresh. There is nothing
#      cached here that can go stale, and no way to make the row green by
#      editing this file — editing the anchor only re-points it at different
#      prose.
#   2. An `assert` row DOES store a value, and that is its honest boundary.
#      It is for a qualitative claim ("the sweep keeps no expected-gate
#      ledger") where no figure appears in the prose. Someone could make such
#      a row green by editing `expected` here while the prose still asserts
#      the old proposition. Prefer `prose`; use `assert` only when the claim
#      states no number.
# EVERY OCCURRENCE OF THE ANCHOR IS CHECKED, NOT THE FIRST. A dead figure
# written in a live figure's clothes is a finding. This repository records
# superseded figures in prose deliberately, so an anchor must be specific
# enough to match only the LIVE assertion — that specificity is the row
# author's job, and a too-loose anchor surfaces as a FALSE, not as silence.
# FORMAT — TSV, TAB-separated, field 1 is the row type from a closed set.
#   surface  <path>
#       A declared "advertised surface" per §11.4.266(A). Claims may only be
#       registered against a declared surface.
#   claim  <id>  <surface>  <kind>  <bluff-type>  <severity>  <op>  <expected>  <anchor>  <probe>
#       id          stable ASCII slug, unique in this file
#       surface     must equal a declared `surface` path
#       kind        `prose`  — anchor MUST carry exactly one capture group; the
#                              captured text is the CLAIMED value, compared
#                              against the probe's output. `expected` is `-`.
#                   `assert` — anchor carries no capture group and only proves
#                              the claim is still made; the probe's output is
#                              compared against `expected`.
#       bluff-type  one of the SEVEN-member closed vocabulary of §11.4.266(B):
#                     green-but-broken  coverage-theater  rubber-stamp-verified
#                     stubbed-core      doc-vs-code-drift
#                     config-present-but-unwired            byte-identical-fork
#                   An ad-hoc type is a FAIL, never a silent pass. The type is
#                   a ROUTING KEY to the counter-gate that owns the type
#       severity    consumer-supplied DATA per §11.4.266(B) — the corpus states
#                   no scale. Here: blocker | major | minor.
#       op          `eq`      claimed == real, after whitespace trim
#                   `ne`      claimed != real
#                   `matches` real matches the ERE in the claimed/expected slot
#       expected    `assert` rows only; `-` for `prose`
#       anchor      a Python `re` pattern matched against the surface file with
#                   DOTALL off and MULTILINE on
#       probe       a shell command, run fresh with cwd = repository root. Its
#                   stdout is the REALITY. A non-zero exit is UNDETERMINED —
#                   never a pass, never a finding.
# COVERAGE IS BOUNDED AND SAID SO. This slice is TEN rows. §11.4.266(A)
# requires EVERY advertised capability to resolve to exactly one row, and that
# is NOT satisfied here. `bash scripts/verify-claim-ledger.sh --completeness`
# counts the unregistered countable-claim shapes on the declared surfaces and
# reports them as waves. Do not read a green exit as ledger completeness.
surface
surface
surface
surface
surface
# The four carriers are byte-identical from the measured convergence line down
# and `verify-governance-cascade.sh` check C5 enforces that, so a claim in the
# shared region is advertised FOUR TIMES by four files that cannot legally
# disagree. Each such claim is registered ONCE, against `CLAUDE.md`, and the
# other three are covered by C5's byte-identity rather than by a row here.
# THE HONEST BOUNDARY OF THAT CHOICE, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: if C5 were
# ever to go red, this gate would still be reading only `CLAUDE.md`, so a
# now-false claim surviving in `AGENTS.md` alone would be invisible HERE. The
# two gates are complements and neither substitutes for the other. `AGENTS.md`,
# `QWEN.md` and `GEMINI.md` are declared surfaces above so that a claim unique
# to one of them — anything above the convergence line — can be registered
# without first amending this file.
claim
claim
claim
claim
claim
claim
claim
claim
claim
column10: for N in $(seq 1 60); do c=$(for f in CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md QWEN.md GEMINI.md; do tail -n +$N "$f" | sha256sum; done | sort -u | wc -l); if [ "$c" = 1 ]; then echo "$N"; break; fi; done
